## 2A

```{r }
growdata <-read_csv("C:\\Users\\lbmoy2\\Downloads\\Growth curves data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)



growdata %>%
  group_by(Taxon) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(Mass), sd = sd(Mass))

```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
meanv <- c(0,0,0,0)
  cumsum <- 0
for(i in 1 : 4){

  countD = 0
  for (j in 1:20) {
    if (growdata$`Taxon ID`[j] == i) {
      countD <- countD + 1
    }
  }

  meanv[i] <- mean(growdata$Mass[1:countD])
  cumsum <- cumsum+ countD
  print(countD)
  print(cumsum)
}
```


## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
g <-ggplot(growdata, aes(x = Age, y = Mass, shape = Taxon))
g + geom_point()

lm(formula = log(Mass) ~ log(Age), data = growdata)
```

T-rex seems to be the most different compared to the rest of the taxons. T-rex looks like it has the larger mass and grows at a higher rate compared to the rest of the taxons. The other taxons look relative in terms of avg mass and growth rate. Maybe Albertosaurus is larger.

Linear: A dino at age 0 will have a mass of 9.92 or e^2.295. Every one year increase in age will result in a mass increase of 5.78
